$description: The DBIM colour system, transcribed from the DBIM ToolKit 'Colours' chapter (https://dbimtoolkit.digifootprint.gov.in/dbim-chapters?slug=colours) on 2026-08-11. The page is a JS-rendered SPA behind a login, so it cannot be fetched programmatically — these values were read from a screenshot of the rendered chapter and cross-checked against docs/source-brd/MoSJE DBIM Audit.pdf, which independently reproduces the Blue group (p.14) and the Linen background rule (p.15). TRANSCRIBED, NOT DERIVED: every hex here is DBIM's own. Do not regenerate these from an anchor — a conformance palette that has been re-derived is no longer a conformance palette.

$source.corroboratedBy: docs/source-brd/MoSJE DBIM Audit.pdf (Blue group p.14; Linen #EBEAEA p.15; key-colour rules p.16)

primaryPalette.$description: Figure 1 — six colour groups, five shades each, ordered 1 (darkest) to 5 (lightest). Shade 1 is the GROUP'S KEY COLOUR.
$rules: Only ONE colour group may be selected from the primary palette.
The selected group should best represent the organisation's primary functions and objectives.
If the entity has an established brand colour, the group should complement and enhance it.
Colour usage must ensure accessibility of the digital platform.
The selected colour group is mandated for DIGITAL PLATFORMS ONLY.
Gradients may use any two variants from the selected group (Figure 2).

functionalPalette.$description: Table 1 — applies across functional elements (text, background, status) regardless of which primary group is selected.

linen.use: Background to highlight images. Background for quotes or text needing special attention. Outlines to boxes and components.

inclusive.use: Primary page background. Headshot background. Text over a dark background. Icon on a dark background. State Emblem on a dark background. Cookie consent banner background.

deepEarthyBrown.use: Text colour over a light background such as Inclusive white or Linen.

black.use: State Emblem of India on a light background.

deepBlue.use: Gov.In root website identity only — NOT for departmental platforms.

blue.use: Status colour for INFORMATION. Also the hyperlink colour, in addition to the key colour of the selected group.

$notesForImplementers: DBIM's greys are PURE neutrals — R=G=B, chroma exactly 0. If a DBIM mode is implemented, its neutrals must not be tinted with the primary hue the way the blue/navy brands are.

DBIM's status colours differ from the estate's: Liberty Green #198754 vs our success #046A38; Mustard Yellow #FFC107 vs our warning; Coral Red #DC3545 vs our danger; Blue #0D6EFD vs our info. A DBIM mode that repaints only the primary ramp is NOT DBIM-conformant — the functional palette moves too.

DBIM publishes five shades per group; this estate's ramps have eleven rungs. Pin the five DBIM values at the rungs their lightness lands on and interpolate the rest; never re-derive a published shade.
Text over light backgrounds is Deep Earthy Brown #150202, not black and not a neutral step.
Deep Blue #1D0A69 is reserved for the Gov.In root site. Do not use it in a departmental palette.
